svg.aria-label: The five steps of thyroid hormone synthesis: follicle and colloid structure, iodide concentration by the sodium iodide symporter, organification and coupling by thyroid peroxidase, the stored form on thyroglobulin, and conversion of T4 to active T3 by deiodinase in target tissue.
svg.text: A Follicle: the cell faces blood on one side and colloid on the other
BLOOD
Follicular cell
COLLOID (lumen of the follicle)
thyroglobulin: a large protein rich in tyrosine
NIS
I- in
1 Trapping: active uptake, concentrated more than 30-fold
2 Thyroglobulin is made and secreted into the colloid
TPO
3 Organification: TPO oxidises I- and attaches it
to tyrosine: MIT (one I) and DIT (two I)
4 Coupling, also by TPO:
DIT + DIT = T4 MIT + DIT = T3
stored on thyroglobulin until needed
5 TSH makes the cell take colloid back; lysosomes free T3 and T4
B T4 is the circulating form; T3 is the active one
T4 (about 90%)
deiodinase
T3 (active)
T3 binds the nuclear receptor about 10 times more tightly.
Long T4 half-life keeps blood levels steady; each tissue sets its own deiodinase.
